messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER @Priya (SRE) — high severity alert: spike in TLS handshake failures in prod-east-1 starting at ~10:41 UTC. Please acknowledge.
Samir (oncall): acked and joining bridge. What's the customer impact?
Helen (support): seeing multiple real-user reports — a few enterprise orgs and some self-serve users. Error pattern: 502/503 and occasional `tls: bad certificate` from reverse proxy logs. Dashboard: /v1/generate errors up to ~35% in east-1 over the last 8 minutes.
Priya (SRE): I'm pulling proxy and edge logs now. Kicking off `journalctl -u lb-proxy --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -i tls` and tcpdump on the front-line nodes.
Maya (eng): please paste samples if you see `first record does not look like a TLS handshake` vs `bad certificate` — those point to very different root causes.
Priya (SRE): snippets from logs:
```
2026-04-12T10:41:12Z lb-edge[pid]: WARN tls: handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-04-12T10:41:13Z haproxy[pid]: SSL: recv handshake: tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake
2026-04-12T10:41:20Z cert-rotator[controller]: ERROR rotate job timed out: context deadline exceeded
2026-04-12T10:42:00Z kernel: IN=eth0 OUT= MAC=.. SRC=54.210.33.4 DST=10.20.2.11 PROTO=ICMP TYPE=3 CODE=4 (frag needed and DF set) MTU=1500
```
Jorge (netinfra): I just saw a config change in the peering automation this morning: `peering-rollout-2026-04-12` pushed at 09:45 UTC. It updated transit MTU to 9000 on some border nodes to enable jumbo frames. Could be relevant.
Priya (SRE): tcpdump shows fragments and ICMP frag-needed on some flows during handshake. Sample capture (redacted):
```
10:41:11.900 IP 54.210.33.4.51200 > 10.20.2.11.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
10:41:11.910 IP 10.20.2.11.443 > 54.210.33.4.51200: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
10:41:11.920 IP (frag) 10.20.2.11 > 54.210.33.4: frag off 0, id 2468
10:41:11.925 IP 54.210.33.4 > 10.20.2.11: ICMP Frag needed, mtu 1500
10:41:11.930 IP 54.210.33.4.51200 > 10.20.2.11.443: Flags [R]
```
Maya (eng): that ICMP pattern plus a long cert chain can break some clients — if the server's CERT message crosses an MTU boundary and the client can't handle reassembly or path MTU discovery fails, the client may reset. Did the cert-rotator change the chain length?
Priya (SRE): cert-rotator logs show new cert bundles being assembled at 10:30 UTC with 5 intermediates (previous default was 2). Also saw `rotate job timed out` messages.
Helen (support): customers report retries sometimes succeed when routed to west-2. Region fallback seems to mitigate for now.
Samir (oncall): start mitigations: 1) rollback cert-rotator to stable tag `cert-rot-20260410-stable`; 2) enforce TCP MSS clamp on east-1 transit to 1400; 3) pause peering MTU jumbo rollout. Someone run the commands for MSS clamp and the rollback.
Jorge (netinfra): applying MSS clamp to transit routers (example commands):
```
# pseudo-config
set policy-options policy-statement clamp-mss term 1 then set tcp-mss 1400
commit and-quit
```
Jorge (netinfra): pausing MTU change via rollout controller, rolling back the jumbo MTU on the subset of edges that were updated.
Priya (SRE): cert-rotator rollback initiated at 10:51 UTC, controllers report successful restart and certificates replaced with prior bundle.
IncidentBot: Incident severity changed to SEV2 based on partial impact reduction. On-call handoff queued: Samir -> Jorge in 20m.
Priya (SRE): after rollback + MSS clamp we see error rate drop from 35% to ~5% over 15 minutes. Some intermittent 502s remain for ~10 customers.
Maya (eng): preliminary hypotheses: H1 (primary): combination of larger cert chains from cert-rotator + MTU asymmetry (9000 vs 1500) causing fragmentation and ICMP-generated resets during TLS handshake. H2: cert-rotator produced invalid/expired certs for a subset of hosts (less likely; rollback helped). H3: routing change created asymmetric path that drops ICMP required for PMTU and causes timeouts (possible).
Priya (SRE): adding timeline here for RCA tracking: 
- 09:45 UTC — peering-rollout-2026-04-12 started (MTU->9000 on many border links)
- 10:30 UTC — cert-rotator release `cert-rot-20260412` begins rollout in prod-east-1
- 10:36 UTC — VPC peering route refresh applied (automated change)
- 10:41 UTC — spike in TLS handshake failures seen by monitoring and users
- 10:51 UTC — cert-rotator rollback initiated
- 11:00 UTC — MSS clamp and MTU rollback applied to affected transit nodes
- 11:07 UTC — error rates substantially decreased, monitoring in watch window
Jorge (netinfra): digging into path MTU discovery behaviour — some intermediate devices had DF=1 and either dropped fragments or rate-limited ICMP. I'll capture traceroutes with `--mtu` flags and run targeted `mtr` checks.
Priya (SRE): packet snippet shows server sending a large ServerHello+Certificate fragment that triggered ICMP from an intermediate hop with MTU 1500 while server path had 9000 possible:
```
# server->client large TCP payload segmented into IP fragments
IP (frag) len=8200 id=5892 off=0 frag
ICMP frag-needed TTL=... MTU=1500
```
Helen (support): customer impact summary: roughly 14 orgs impacted, two enterprise customers saw >90s of sustained failures triggering potential SLA hits. I'm drafting customer comms and adding to the incident ticket.
Samir (oncall): create a formal incident ticket and attach these artifacts + pcap. Priya please own ticket creation.
Priya (SRE): INC-2026-0412-07 created and linked to this thread with pcap and initial timeline.
IncidentBot: INC-2026-0412-07 assigned to prod-east-1 SRE rotation. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0412-07
Maya (eng): immediate follow-ups we should track in the RCA: 1) change cert-rotator to produce minimal chained bundles by default and add a unit/regression test to validate chain length; 2) add canary gating to MTU changes across peering links; 3) instrument edge proxies to log cert chain lengths and TLS record sizes; 4) update runbooks for MSS clamp and MTU rollback steps.
Jorge (netinfra): action items (in-thread):
- [NET-1] full path MTU matrix and list of affected prefixes (owner: Jorge, due +12h)
- [NET-2] add preflight check to peering rollout to detect asymmetric MTU (owner: Infra team, due +72h)
- [CERT-1] adjust cert-rotator to prefer trimmed bundles + add max-chain config (owner: Maya, due +48h)
- [SRE-1] document emergency MSS clamp runbook and automation (owner: Priya, due +24h)
- [COMM-1] support to send post-incident customer summary and SLA assessment (owner: Helen, due +24h)
Priya (SRE): monitoring window started. Will update ticket and this thread with final RCA draft.
Samir (oncall): handing primary to Jorge in 20m. I'll remain on-call if escalation needed. Good job team.
Jorge (netinfra): acknowledged. Moving this thread to RCA workspace — will update with pcap analysis and definitive root cause.
IncidentBot: Handoff complete. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes or on major change.
